hypotheses.justification: Nothing in the statement needs this instance to elaborate: `indK0`, `ExactK0.of`, `FGModuleCat.of`, `Nat.factorization` and `relIndex` don't use it. It follows from the other hypotheses except when p = 0, and the statement is trivially true when p = 0. `CharP.char_is_prime_or_zero` (Mathlib/Algebra/CharP/Defs.lean) needs only `[Nontrivial k]` and `[NoZeroDivisors k]`, which `[Field k]` provides. Together with `[CharP k p]` it gives `p.Prime ∨ p = 0`. The proof splits on this. (1) If `p.Prime`, set `haveI : Fact p.Prime := ⟨hp⟩` and run the existing proof unchanged. (2) If `p = 0`, take `D := C`. Then `D ≤ C` is `le_rfl`. Since 0 is not prime, `Nat.factorization_eq_zero_of_not_prime` gives `(Nat.card C).factorization 0 = 0`, so `0 ^ 0 = 1`. `Subgroup.relIndex_self` gives `C.relIndex C = 1`, which settles the index condition. `¬ 0 ∣ Nat.card C` holds because `0 ∣ n ↔ n = 0` and `Nat.card C > 0`: C is finite because of `[Finite G]`, and nonempty. The induced-class equation becomes `x = 1 • x`, which is `one_smul`. So the theorem stays true and provable after `omit [Fact p.Prime] in`.
